Both edits applied cleanly. The pointer in SKILL.md now flags the yield-spread variant and routes to the detailed reference.

Summary of what I saved (and why it's generalizable, not per-question trivia):

The question itself was answered correctly, but it exposed a distinct sub-pattern not previously documented in the skill: **averaging a yield SPREAD across a multi-year monthly window** from the Treasury Bulletin's interest-rate/bond-yield tables. Three generalizable lessons captured:

1. **Spread = difference of two columns per month** — the metric isn't a single printed cell; read both yield series and subtract per month, then average. (Noted that mean-of-differences == difference-of-means as a cross-check.)
2. **Multi-year window divisor** — "CY1960-1969" = ~120 monthly rows, not 12; partial-year reads silently corrupt the average.
3. **Table/series disambiguation** — these yields live in the bond-yield section (not outlays tables); must match the exact series (Moody's Aa not Aaa; long-term Treasury bond not bills/intermediate).

I added this as a new section in the existing `descriptive-stats-over-months.md` reference (it belongs to the same "read one number per month, compute one stat" family) plus a discoverable pointer in SKILL.md. I used the filesystem patch tool rather than skill_manage since the SKILL.md is >100KB (skill_manage patch is blocked at that size, per my standing memory note). No new memory entry needed — the durable cross-session facts here are procedural and already live in the skill reference.
